exposure.why: no teammate has opened these images (statement pending); the evaluation-time ephemeris was never printed or saved (MOST rule, docs/EXPOSURE.md)

permitted_inputs.name: our own training positions (SPHEREx pixels, A3 fit)
observer: Earth (astropy built-in) plus spacecraft header position
Sun and giant-planet positions (astropy built-in)
permitted_inputs.used_for: frames and the synthetic N-body orbits of the model-error term

permitted_inputs.name: evaluation exposure times (MOST listing, identifiers and times only)

ephemeris_use: JPL positions (MOST) located the training images and guided the training fits (3 arcsec gate); they never enter the orbit fit or the forecast. Evaluation-time positions were never read.

model.uncertainty: v2 envelope (group Monte Carlo, 300 draws, and visit x detector jackknife, along and across the track) + sigma_g^2 + spacecraft term + two-body model error (second moment of 24 synthetic N-body orbits with our fitted a, e, i)
model.start_source: our first-visit positions and motion over geocentric distances 0.8-4.0 AU

baseline.description: straight line in RA/Dec fitted to the same positions

scoring.observed: mean over identified evaluation exposures of observed - model(t_i), east/north arcsec
scoring.c_obs: sample covariance of the residuals / N (N >= 3), never below the mean fit covariance / N
scoring.c_pred: frozen primary covariance at the mean evaluation time
scoring.secondary: the heliocentric forecast and the straight line are scored on the same positions and C_obs

rules: cutouts centred on the frozen primary forecast at each evaluation exposure time (no ephemeris query)
every peak with S/N >= 5 within the listing radius is a candidate and is kept
A3 fit S/N >= 10 within max(15 arcsec, 3 x the largest 1-sigma of C_pred) of the forecast
static check: no source at S/N >= 5 at the same sky position in another exposure of the same detector taken at least 0.5 day apart (a static reference cutout)
two or more passing candidates in one exposure -> ambiguous; motion consistency across exposures (chi-square, p = 0.997, 0.3 arcsec allowance)
